rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Curve sketching is classification before plotting. **Symmetry theorems:** f(−x) = f(x) ⟹ even, mirror in the y-axis (x², cos x); f(−x) = −f(x) ⟹ odd, half-turn about the origin (x³ + x is odd; f(0) = 0 when defined there); parity multiplies like signs, and odd+odd = odd.…

rows.text: ***The compressed wave*** - sin 3x has period 2pi/3: frequency and period are reciprocals, so tripling the frequency thirds the period.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Reading Graphs Like a Pro Before calculus, curve sketching extracts everything from the formula by classification: **symmetry** (odd/even), **periodicity**, **monotonicity**, and intercepts. Each is a theorem-shaped test applied to f's formula.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Symmetry tests (the theorems) - **Even function:** f(−x) = f(x) ⟺ graph symmetric about the **y-axis** (cos x, x²). - **Odd function:** f(−x) = −f(x) ⟺ symmetric about the **origin** (sin x, x³); consequence: f(0) = 0 for odd functions defined at 0. - **Neither** is the common case (e.g. x + x²). **Symmetry about x-axis** (y²-forms) fails the function test unless restricted.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Parity: substitute -x and compare. Period of f(ax): T/|a|. Invertibility: prove strict monotonicity via f(b) - f(a). Intercepts: f(0) and f(x) = 0.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Determine whether f(x) = x³ + x is even, odd, or neither, and state the geometric meaning.** — **Test:** replace x by −x: f(−x) = (−x)³ + (−x) = −x³ − x = **−(x³ + x) = −f(x)**. The odd-function identity holds ⟹ **f is odd**.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Find the period of (i) f(x) = sin 3x and (ii) g(x) = |sin x|.** — **(i)** sin x has period 2π. By the **period-shift theorem**, f(ax + b) has period T/|a|: sin 3x has period 2π/|3| = **2π/3** — tripling the frequency thirds the period. **(ii)** Check T = π: |sin(x + π)| = |−sin x| = |sin x| ✓, so π is a period.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For odd/even questions, write the comparison chain f(-x) -> simplify -> equals f(x) or -f(x) or neither - the verdict needs the simplified middle step.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Symmetry is labour-saving: even graphs need half the sketch, odd graphs a quarter - and parity multiplies like signs.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Even: f(-x) = f(x), symmetric about y-axis (x^2, cos x, |x|). Odd: f(-x) = -f(x), symmetric about origin (x^3, sin x, 1/x); f(0) = 0 if 0 in domain. Parity multiplication: even x even = even, odd x odd = even, even x odd = odd.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: AC electricity is periodic with 50 Hz in Nepal: the period 1/50 s is the period-shift theorem powering the grid's frequency bookkeeping.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Even function** | f(−x) = f(x) — y-axis mirror | x², cos x, |x| | | **Odd function** | f(−x) = −f(x) — origin rotation | x³, sin x, 1/x | | **Period** | Least T > 0 with f(x+T) = f(x) | 2π for sin | | **Monotone** | Steady rise or fall on an interval | eˣ increasing |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why symmetry halves the work - An even graph needs sketching only for x ≥ 0 — mirror the rest. An odd graph needs a quarter's work rotated. Symmetry is labour-saving, not decoration. ### 4.2 The period-shift theorem at work - sin 2x has period 2π/2 = π: doubling the frequency halves the period.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Symmetry tests at a glance** | Test | Equation | Geometry | |---|---|---| | even | f(−x) = f(x) | mirror in y-axis | | odd | f(−x) = −f(x) | half-turn about origin | | neither | both fail | no global symmetry |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Odd ⟹ f(0) = 0:** only when 0 is in the domain — 1/x is odd but undefined at 0.  ·  **Products of parities:** even×even = even, odd×odd = even, even×odd = odd — parity multiplies like signs.  ·  **Period of f(ax):** T/|a|, not aT — compression shrinks the period.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (2m): Determine whether f(x) = x³ + x is even, odd or neither, and interpret geometrically.** — f(−x) = (−x)³ + (−x) = −x³ − x = −(x³ + x) = **−f(x)** ⟹ **odd**: the graph is symmetric about the origin (a 180° rotation maps it onto itself).…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Find the period of (i) sin 3x, (ii) |sin x|.** — (i) sin has period 2π; by the period-shift theorem f(ax) has period 2π/|a|: **π·... 2π/3** for sin 3x. (ii) folding negatives up, |sin(x + π)| = |−sin x| = |sin x|, and no smaller positive T works: **period π** — the fold doubles the repetition rate.  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Show that f(x) = x³ is strictly increasing on ℝ and deduce that it has an inverse.** — Take a < b; then b³ − a³ = (b − a)(b² + ab + a²). The first factor is positive; the second equals (b² + ab + a²) = (a + b/2)²·...…
